question: What are the requirements for the cancellation or suspension of a DDCM or clinical trial by the sponsor?
answer:
The sponsor may suspend or cancel a DDCM or clinical trial at any time, provided they submit the necessary justifications and a follow-up plan for participants, if the trial has already begun [RDC 945/2024, Art. 85]. 

If the cancellation is due to safety reasons, the sponsor must describe the reasons and present measures to minimize or mitigate risks to the participants [RDC 945/2024, Art. 85]. Additionally, these actions must be filed with Anvisa as a secondary petition attached to the respective process within 15 business days of the decision [RDC 945/2024, Art. 85]. 

In cases of temporary suspension as an immediate safety measure, the sponsor must notify Anvisa within 7 calendar days, justifying the reasons and clearly explaining the scope, treatment interruption, and suspension of recruitment [RDC 945/2024, Art. 85]. Once a DDCM is cancelled, no related clinical trial may continue in the country [RDC 945/2024, Art. 85].
